title: Release Manifest — draft 0.1.0
description: Piece 5 of the growth layer: the version-continuity link (NGA v0.2 §5, 'agent identity → release manifest → task/run and decision revisions → ...'). Every field traces to a named §5 sentence. The manifest consists of references to independently managed artifacts — it is NOT a single deployment unit (the string-reference shapes below are that statement). Invariants stated by §5 but not carried per-release (a rollback cannot undo a confirmed credit registration; version pinning cannot preserve revoked rights — live revocation still applies; candidate promotion never silently rewrites an adopted decision) live in this description and are enforced where they have a mechanism: revocation at the adopt gate's 14-A4 recheck, promotion at the replay boundary (piece 6). Provenance: NGA 13号 §5 — 'proposed'; this schema is an evidence-track probe answer.

release_version.description: §5's linking structure names the release manifest as its own link — the format version of this artifact (distinct from the referenced specification versions).

release_id.description: The manifest's own identity in the linking chain (candidate and subsequent release are distinct links).

agent_identity.description: §5 'agent identity → release manifest' — the head of the linking structure.

references.description: §5 'A release manifest references the compatible model/readout versions, semantic and adoption specifications, capability/workflow/graph definitions, context policies, and relevant controller/enforcement contracts.' The four version/spec pins are the manifest's core (minItems 1); the definition/policy/contract categories may be empty — presence of the key is the explicit declaration, and only RELEVANT contracts are referenced.

rollout.description: §5 'Rollout policy must state which new tasks receive a release and what happens to in-flight work.'

new_tasks.description: Which new tasks receive this release — a stated policy, not a default.

in_flight.description: §5's three named choices for in-flight work. Live permission revocation still applies where required — version pinning cannot preserve revoked rights.

rollback.description: §5 'A rollback can change routing for new work or trigger explicit handling of active work. It cannot undo a confirmed credit registration. External effects require their business correction/compensation contract.'

external_effect_correction.description: The business correction/compensation contract reference for external effects — required because a rollback cannot undo them.

evidence.description: §5 'A release can be technically compatible and still fail business acceptance. Keep version compatibility, policy conformance, and measured business improvement as separate evidence.' Three distinct fields, none substituting another.
